Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing our options and answers below; attaching a short KMS options doc and our latest SOC2 report for legal.

Short answers (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers (TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or stronger). All API endpoints require HTTPS and we terminate TLS at the edge.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for persistent storage. Model weights and customer data are encrypted at rest.
- Key management: three supported patterns:
  1) Redwood-managed keys (default): we handle keys (AWS KMS-backed) and rotate per our security policy.
  2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK): customers can supply keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. We support envelope encryption so the customer key encrypts a data key we use for storage.
  3) HSM-backed BYOK (for highest assurance): integrate with customer HSM/KMS for key storage and signing operations (we support PKCS#11-based HSMs + cloud HSM services).
- Key rotation: supports customer-driven rotation schedules; Redwood will respect rotation and re-encrypt data keys as needed (we automate re-wrapping via envelope keys).

Logs & PII:
- Application logs: by default we do NOT log raw customer payloads. Only metadata (request ids, timestamps, route/model used, token counts, error traces) are retained.
- We can provide a hardened logging configuration for Dedicated/Private deployments that excludes any PII fields; we also offer a tokenization/PII-stripping pipeline as an optional pre-store hook for high-risk fields.
- Retention: default metrics/logs retention is 90 days in hosted; Dedicated customers can configure retention down to 7 days or longer depending on contract.

Data residency & routing:
- Region routing: we can pin customer traffic to specific regions (US/EU/APAC) and tenant data is stored in configured regions for Private/Dedicated. Hosted customers can request EU-only tenancy under enterprise contracts.

Next recommended steps:
1) See attached 'redwood_kms_options.pdf' for an architecture overview and recommended patterns based on your compliance needs.
2) Legal: attached 'SOC2-report-2026.pdf' for initial review. If you need an NDA or redaction, let us know.
3) Technical deep-dive: propose a 60-minute session with Dev Patel (SE) to walk through KMS integration and log redaction options — suggested times: Mon 2/22 10am PT or Wed 2/24 9am PT.
4) If PayWise prefers, we can draft contract language around responsibilities for key custody and rotation.

Quick note on responsibilities (we'll formalize in contract):
- Customer responsibility: key custody (if BYOK), granting Redwood necessary wrap/unwrap permissions or HSM access, and managing rotation schedule.
- Redwood responsibility: secure envelope encryption flows, key usage audit logs, access controls on plaintext keys, and data access auditing.

I'll loop Dev on the technical availability.

Alex — quick technical follow-up from our infra team:

- Audit logs: all KMS operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/Wrap/Unwrap) are logged with request IDs, principal, and timestamps. For BYOK we surface a separate key access audit stream that customers can ingest into their SIEM.
- Logs containing request payloads: we have two layers — request tracing (no payload) and request recording (configurable for debugging). Recording is OFF by default for hosted customers. Recording can be enabled in Dedicated with strict ACLs and optional PII redaction.
- PII redaction/tokenization: we offer a pre-ingest hook (lambda-style) that can run customer-provided code or our standard redaction pipeline to replace PII with stable tokens. This keeps downstream logs/token usage non-identifiable.
- Re-encryption performance: envelope re-wrapping jobs are done backgrounded; expect a modest CPU/GPU-free operation with predictable window (hours) depending on dataset size. We can provide benchmarks for your estimated dataset size.

Action items from our side:
- I'll prepare a short checklist of required IAM permissions for AWS KMS and example policy snippets for GCP/Azure.
- I'll also include an example contract clause for key custody and auditing to speed legal review.

Regards,
